roadmap.walking_skeleton: DISTILL named scenario 1, `a declared HUD screen reports the shield charge a downstream test asserts on`, as the skeleton (feature-delta § DISTILL / Walking-skeleton strategy) and it is RED at scaffold — unlike progress-bar, whose skeleton was already satisfied by reuse. It is the Phase-3.5-adapted API demo: GameUI is a library with no CLI, so the driving port IS the public API and the observable output is the returned array (`bars[0].label == "Shield charge"`, `bars[0].value == 0.65`, `collectTexts == ["SYSTEMS", "Shields"]`). No subprocess is fabricated. Every layer the feature ships is on its path: childViews' composite branch, its container branch, collect's recursion, and two convenience wrappers. Because it ends in a convenience, it turns green at 01-02 rather than 01-01 — the skeleton is the LAST scenario of phase 01, not the first. That is a consequence of the dependency direction (conveniences call collect, collect calls childViews), not an ordering choice: no step can demonstrate the skeleton earlier without pulling `collectProgressBars` and `collectTexts` forward into 01-01 and leaving the other three conveniences behind, which would split one file across two steps for no test-visible gain. 01-01 nonetheless ends with 33 of the 42 RED tests green, including the whole of Slice 2, so it is a working walking skeleton of the traversal core with only the naming layer outstanding.
roadmap.sizing_rationale:
THREE steps by evidence from distill/red-classification.md, not by preference for granularity. The count is defended in both directions.

WHY 01-01 CANNOT BE SPLIT (childViews and collect are one step, not two). Of the 42 RED tests, exactly TWO turn green from `childViews` alone — `every child-bearing view type reports at least one child` and `no registered leaf type traps when asked for its children`, the only tests in the suite that never call `collect`. ZERO tests turn green from `collect` alone. The other 40 need both. Every Slice 2 child-bearing test asserts BOTH halves in the same test body (`childViews(of: stack).count == 2` AND `sentinelIDs(in: stack) == [...]`, where `sentinelIDs` calls `collect`), and every Slice 2 leaf test pairs `childViews(of: leaf).isEmpty` with a `collect` positive control — deliberately, per the vacuous-green audit in red-classification.md § 'why 5 tests were rewritten mid-wave'. A childViews-only step would therefore green 2 of 42 tests and leave the skeleton red; a collect-only step is not constructible at all. The smallest honest unit is both.

WHY 01-02 IS SEPARATE (the conveniences are not padding). Slice 1 splits 9/9 on this line. Nine scenarios (2, 3, 4, 8, 9, 10, 15, 16, 17) call `collect` directly and go green at 01-01. Nine (1, 5, 6, 7, 11, 12, 13, 14, 18) are gated solely on the five conveniences and cannot go green before 01-02. That is a separate file, a separate group of five driving-port rows in DESIGN § Driving Ports, and it carries a design commitment of its own — the deliberate `collectTexts`/`collectTextColors` asymmetry (scenario 13), which DESIGN documents and DISTILL pinned with two adjacent tests specifically so a future tidy-up has to argue with a red test. Folding it into 01-01 would make a single TDD cycle span three files and 42 tests, which is larger than anything this project has done in one step.

WHY 02-01 IS SEPARATE. It has no acceptance test behind it, changes a different artifact class (workflow YAML, not Swift), and is verified by a different command (`act`/CI run and local shell reproduction, not `swift test`). It is the feature's PRIMARY enforcement mechanism per ADR-006 Decision 3 — burying it inside a TDD cycle whose gate is `swift test` would hide a design-compliance obligation behind a test run that cannot observe it. It does have `files_to_modify` (`.forgejo/workflows/ci.yml`), so it is not a validation-only step.

DECOMPOSITION RATIO: 3 steps / 4 production files = 0.75, well inside the 2.5 ceiling. `Package.swift` is already edited by DISTILL and is deliberately absent from every step.

WHAT WAS REJECTED. A four-step split adding 'remove the __SCAFFOLD__ markers' as its own step: marker removal is part of finishing each file and has no independent gate. A slice-shaped split (Slice 1 step, Slice 2 step): Slice 2's 24 RED tests all go green at 01-01 while half of Slice 1 does not, so the slice boundary and the code boundary do not coincide — following it would produce two steps that each half-implement the same two files.

steps.implementation_notes:
BRANCH ORDER IS NORMATIVE, NOT STYLISTIC (ADR-006 Decision 2, brief.md § Traversal Contract). The first seven branches mirror `LayoutEngine.layoutNode` (LayoutEngine.swift:35-67) exactly, in this order:

    Text → HasFrameSize → AnyButton → ZStackView → WrappedText → ContainerView
      → AnyDirectionalPaddingModifier → ChildrenProviding → composite body → []

`ChildrenProviding` is the one branch `layoutNode` does NOT have (DDD-9) and it returns `viewChildren`. The chain ends with `if V.Body.self != Never.self { return [view.body] }` and then `return []`. Accessors, all already public, no access widening anywhere: `HasFrameSize.framedContent`, `AnyButton.anyContent`, `ZStackView.zStackChildren`, `ContainerView.containerChildren`, `AnyDirectionalPaddingModifier.paddingContent`, `ChildrenProviding.viewChildren`. `Text` and `WrappedText` return `[]` — their LayoutNode children are generated geometry, not views.

DO NOT add a branch for the deprecated `AnyPaddingModifier`. `PaddingModifier` conforms to both and is reached through `AnyDirectionalPaddingModifier`; a second padding branch would resurrect the dispatch-order fragility ADR-003 closed. `ViewTraversalSlice2CoverageTests` asserts this shape directly in `PaddingModifier reports its padded content and the sentinel inside is reached`.

`childViews` MUST stay generic over `V: View`. `Body` is an associated type, so inside a function typed `any View` the `.body` branch is unreachable — that is the exact trap that produced both field incidents. Call sites may still hold `any View`: Swift opens the existential implicitly at a generic parameter (DDD-8).

COLLECT'S RECURSION AND ODQ-VT-09. Recurse with a `for` loop over a NAMED binding, not a closure:

    var result: [T] = []
    if let match = view as? T { result.append(match) }
    for child in childViews(of: view) { result += collect(type, from: child) }
    return result

ODQ-VT-09 (recorded at DISTILL so DELIVER does not rediscover it): passing a TUPLE ELEMENT of an implicitly-typed closure parameter to a generic parameter defeats implicit existential opening and fails with `type 'any View' cannot conform to 'View'` (#ProtocolTypeNonConformance). A bare `any View` element in a `for` loop is fine, which is the shape above and the shape the two Slice 2 aggregate tests already use.

NO CYCLE GUARD AND NO DEPTH CAP (ODQ-VT-04, decided at DESIGN, confirmed at DISTILL). The exposure is inherited verbatim from `layoutNode`; a cap on `collect` alone would make the two disagree about the same tree. `collecting from a view whose body contains itself terminates rather than hanging` asserts the process exits `.failure` — adding a guard that returns `[]` instead would turn that test red and violate the documented precondition in the ViewTraversal.swift header.

ZERO CASTS IN GameUITesting (ADR-006 Consequences, 'Constraint created'). `collect` performs no dispatch of its own; all traversal knowledge stays in `GameUI.childViews(of:)`. A fourth chain in `GameUITesting` would sit in the one place the registry check does not look. Step 02-01 adds the CI grep that enforces this; until then, check it by eye.

SCAFFOLD MARKERS — COUNT DISCREPANCY, READ THIS. `distill/red-classification.md` § 'Known, intentional CI failure' says 'DELIVER removes all SIX markers'. That number is WRONG. There are EIGHT `__SCAFFOLD__` occurrences across three files — 2 in ViewTraversal.swift (lines 100 and 107, both inside the one scaffold comment), 1 in Collect.swift, 5 in Conveniences.swift — which is what the DISTILL § Scaffolds table says and what the repo contains. This step removes 3 of the 8; 01-02 removes the other 5. The `constraints` job greps for the literal string and fails on ANY occurrence, so verify with `grep -rc '__SCAFFOLD__' Sources/` and expect zero after 01-02, not after this step.

DO NOT MODIFY `LayoutEngine.swift`, `HitTest.swift`, `View.swift`, `Containers.swift`, `LeafViews.swift`, `ViewBuilder.swift`, `WrappedText.swift`, `ProgressBar.swift` or any other pre-existing source file (DDD-11, ADR-006 Decision 4). Zero existing source files modified is this feature's regression guarantee, verified by `git diff --stat` at review. `layoutNode` deliberately keeps its own chain: it cannot consume a children list, because every branch recurses with branch-specific constraints, origin and node assembly. Resist the pull to 'unify while you are in there' — that is ODQ-VT-06, deliberately deferred. Equally, do NOT fix ODQ-VT-03 (a bare TupleViewN lays out as an empty box) while writing the ChildrenProviding branch; the layout half stays broken by design and the `AbilityRow` fixture says so in its comment.

DO NOT MODIFY `Package.swift` — DISTILL already added the `GameUITesting` target, the `.library` product and the test-target dependency. No further build-graph work exists in this feature.

DO NOT MODIFY ANY TEST FILE. All 43 tests are DISTILL artifacts and are the specification.

Constraints from CLAUDE.md: Swift 6.2, no `import Foundation`, `Float` geometry only (nothing here is numeric, so the CGFloat/Double gate passes trivially), Swift Testing with backtick-quoted names, value types only. `GameUITesting` is SHIPPED code and is bound by all of them identically — it is a plain `.target`, not a `.testTarget`. Never write `@testable import GameUI` in `Sources/GameUITesting/`: it needs `-enable-testing`, which SwiftPM does not apply to a package consumed as a release dependency, so it would compile here and fail at every consumer (ADR-006 Alternative E).

MUTATION TESTING: skipped per CLAUDE.md § Mutation Testing Strategy (Muter is not reliably available in this environment).

EXEMPT FROM PARADIGM (Hypothesis form): this is a Swift package with zero third-party dependencies permitted, so Hypothesis `@given` strategies and `assert_state_delta` do not exist here — see CLAUDE.md § nWave Standing Exemptions, which settles this repo-wide. No seeded sweep either, and that is a judgement DISTILL recorded rather than an omission: this contract is STRUCTURAL over a closed, enumerable domain of 19 view types, so the right instrument is exhaustive enumeration, which is exactly what Slice 2 is. Random sampling would be ceremony over a domain already covered exhaustively. The universe is trivially closed: `childViews` and `collect` are pure return-only functions over an immutable value tree with an empty declared mutation set, no driven ports and no I/O (Principle 12 contract shape: pure-function; DESIGN § Driven Ports + Adapters states this explicitly). There is no state delta to declare.

Run: `swift test --disable-sandbox` (the flag is an environment constraint, not a code defect). Expect 218 tests, 9 issues remaining — all in `ViewTraversalSlice1CollectTests`, all naming a convenience that 01-02 implements.

steps.implementation_notes:
THE ASYMMETRY IS THE SPECIFICATION, NOT A BUG TO TIDY. `collectTexts` covers `Text` AND `WrappedText`; `collectTextColors` covers `Text` ONLY. It is inherited verbatim from the field helper this target replaces and retained deliberately: `WrappedText` carries one `color` for all of its lines, so a merged colour list could not be zipped against the content list (DESIGN § Driving Ports; ADR-006 Decision 1). Two adjacent tests pin it — `collectTexts reports both Text and WrappedText content` and `collectTextColors reports colours for Text only and leaves WrappedText out` — precisely so a future tidy-up has to argue with a red test. Do not 'fix' it.

ORDER TRAP IN collectTexts — A VACUOUSLY-PASSING IMPLEMENTATION EXISTS, DO NOT WRITE IT. The obvious spelling is

    collect(Text.self, from: view).map(\.content) + collect(WrappedText.self, from: view).map(\.content)

and it passes every test in the suite, because no fixture interleaves a WrappedText BEFORE a Text. It nonetheless violates the documented contract in the function's own doc comment (`in declaration order`) for any tree that does interleave them — a helper that returns the right answer on the fixtures and a subtly wrong one in the field is exactly the bug class this feature exists to eliminate, reproduced inside the fix. Walk once instead and preserve order, e.g. `collect((any View).self, from: view).compactMap { ... }` mapping `Text.content` and `WrappedText.content` over a single depth-first pass. This still contains no dispatch to a child-bearing protocol, so the ADR-006 no-cast constraint holds.

The other four are genuinely one-liners over `collect`: `collect((any AnyButton).self, from:)`, `collect(Text.self, from:).map(\.color)`, `collect(ProgressBar.self, from:)`, `collect(Texture.self, from:)`. `each convenience agrees with the collect call it wraps` asserts exactly that equivalence, with a positive control first — 'both sides are empty' is agreement of the useless kind and is what the original bug produced.

NO TRAVERSAL, NO CASTS. `Sources/GameUITesting/` must contain no `as?` cast to `ContainerView`, `ZStackView`, `AnyButton`, `HasFrameSize`, `AnyDirectionalPaddingModifier` or `ChildrenProviding` (ADR-006 Consequences). Step 02-01 makes this a CI gate.

DELETE ALL FIVE `__SCAFFOLD__` MARKERS in this file. Combined with the three removed in 01-01 that is all eight; `grep -rc '__SCAFFOLD__' Sources/` must now report zero, which is what turns the `constraints` CI job green on this branch for the first time. (Note again that red-classification.md § 'Known, intentional CI failure' says 'six markers' — it is wrong; there are eight.)

DO NOT MODIFY any pre-existing source file, any test file, or `Package.swift`. See 01-01.

Constraints from CLAUDE.md: Swift 6.2, no `import Foundation`, `Float` geometry only, value types only. `GameUITesting` is shipped code, never `@testable`.

MUTATION TESTING: skipped per CLAUDE.md § Mutation Testing Strategy.

EXEMPT FROM PARADIGM (Hypothesis form): as 01-01 — Swift package, zero third-party dependencies, CLAUDE.md § nWave Standing Exemptions settles it repo-wide. Contract shape: pure-function (return-only), empty declared mutation set, no driven ports, so no state delta to declare. Compensating coverage is the exhaustive structural enumeration in Slice 2 plus the nine convenience scenarios here.

steps.implementation_notes:
THE REGISTRY STEP IS VERBATIM. Copy the YAML block under brief.md § Architectural Enforcement / 'The traversal registry CI step, verbatim' exactly as written, including its comments — the allowlist comment explaining `extension Never: View` and naming the SwiftSyntax revisit trigger (ADR-006 Alternative G) is load-bearing documentation, not decoration. It runs on alpine with no Swift toolchain, in seconds, in the job's established style. Expected output on the current corpus: `OK — traversal registry covers all 19 View-conforming types` (18 declared + the Never allowlist entry). DISTILL already executed this step locally against the authored registry — 19 declared, 19 registered, 0 missing, 0 stale — so a failure here means a transcription error, not a registry error.

TRANSCRIPTION TRAP IN THE SECOND GREP — READ BEFORE COPYING. The no-dispatch-cast rule appears in brief.md § Architectural Enforcement as a table row, so its alternation is written with markdown-escaped pipes:

    as\? *(any )?(ContainerView\|ZStackView\|AnyButton\|HasFrameSize\|AnyDirectionalPaddingModifier\|ChildrenProviding)

Those `\|` are MARKDOWN table-cell escapes. Under `grep -E` the alternation operator is a bare `|`; a backslash-escaped pipe is not alternation, so the pattern copied literally would never match anything and the gate would pass forever without checking. That is this feature's own bug class — a check that returns the reassuring answer without doing the work — reproduced inside its enforcement. Unescape them. The step is:

      - name: No traversal dispatch in GameUITesting
        run: |
          # ADR-006 Consequences, 'Constraint created'. All traversal knowledge lives in
          # GameUI.childViews(of:). A fourth dispatch chain here would sit in the one
          # place the traversal registry check does not look.
          if grep -rnE 'as\? *(any )?(ContainerView|ZStackView|AnyButton|HasFrameSize|AnyDirectionalPaddingModifier|ChildrenProviding)' \
               --include='*.swift' Sources/GameUITesting/; then
            echo "ERROR: traversal dispatch in Sources/GameUITesting/ — forbidden by ADR-006"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "OK — no traversal dispatch in GameUITesting"

PROVE THE GREP CAN FIRE BEFORE TRUSTING IT. Temporarily add `let x = someView as? any ContainerView` to Collect.swift, run the step, confirm it exits 1, then revert. A negative gate that has never been observed failing is not a gate. This is the same standing rule DISTILL applied to the test suite ('no negative assertion without a positive control').

WHY THIS SECOND GREP IS IN SCOPE despite the DESIGN § Component Decomposition row saying the CI change is 'one step'. That row and brief.md § Architectural Enforcement disagree. The Enforcement table assigns the no-dispatch-cast rule to 'CI (constraints job)' and ADR-006 Consequences records it as a created constraint 'Enforced by CI grep' — but no step implementing it exists anywhere, and DISTILL only ran it by hand (red-classification.md § Gate verdict). Shipping the feature without it would leave a documented constraint enforced by nothing. Explicit justification for the extra step, per the design-compliance rule: it modifies no file outside the one already in the Component Decomposition table (.forgejo/workflows/ci.yml, constraints job), and it discharges an obligation ADR-006 states in its own Consequences section.

TEST-LINUX STEP. Add `swift build -c release --product GameUITesting` after the existing `swift build --build-tests`. brief.md marks it RECOMMENDED and DISTILL's handoff repeats the instruction. It is the ONLY gate that catches a regression to `.testTarget` or a reintroduced `@testable import GameUI`: both compile fine under `--build-tests` and both break every downstream consumer, which is the one place the target has to work. Cost is one incremental release build on a job that already has a Swift toolchain.

ODQ-VT-07 — RESOLVED HERE: NO. The registry check keeps scanning `Sources/GameUI/` only; it is NOT widened to `Sources/GameUITesting/`. Four reasons, in descending weight. (1) Widening would make one module's comment block authoritative over another module's declarations — the same knowledge-locality objection ADR-006 rejected Alternative A on, merely inverted. (2) The realistic failure mode is not 'GameUITesting declares a View type', it is 'GameUITesting grows a traversal chain', and the no-dispatch-cast grep added in this step covers that directly and by name. (3) A child-bearing View type declared in GameUITesting could not work anyway: it would need a `layoutNode` branch it has no way to add — ADR-006 Alternative C's argument applies unchanged — and a composite one is handled free by the `V.Body.self != Never.self` fallback with no registry entry required, exactly as the test-target fixtures `ShieldPanel`, `AbilityRow` and `SentinelComposite` already are. (4) GameUITesting is a two-file module of five wrappers whose charter forbids traversal; a `View` declaration appearing there is a review-visible event, not a silent one. Cost of reversing is one path added to the grep. TRIGGER TO REVISIT, and record it: the first `: View` conformance declared anywhere under `Sources/GameUITesting/`. Record this verdict as a comment ABOVE the `- name: Traversal registry covers every View type` line — outside the `run:` block, so the verbatim step stays byte-for-byte verbatim — and add the resolution row to the feature-delta § Open Questions table.

DO NOT touch the three existing `constraints` steps, the checkout steps, the `test-macos` job, or any runner/container declaration. In particular do not add `--disable-sandbox` to the CI `swift test` invocations: that flag is a local-environment constraint (CLAUDE.md § Running Tests), and both CI jobs pass without it today.

DO NOT modify Sources/, Tests/ or Package.swift in this step. If a registry line turns out to be wrong, that is a phase-01 defect — fix it there and re-run phase 01's gate, rather than loosening the check to accommodate it.

STRUCTURAL VERIFICATION (mandatory, configuration deliverable): this step ships workflow YAML, not application code, so the unit-test paradigm mandate does not apply. Verify structurally instead — run all three new gates locally from the repository root, observe the registry check's `OK` line with the count 19, observe the no-dispatch-cast grep exit 1 on clean sources AND exit 0 on a deliberately planted cast that is then reverted, and confirm a green CI run on the feature branch covering all three jobs.

MUTATION TESTING: not applicable — no application code changes in this step.
